proofs.proof_tex:
The positive conditional assertion is set-theoretic.  For every \(\mathsf P\in\mathfrak M_H\), \(\text{thm:confidence-polytope}\) gives
\[
 \{((r_{bt}),(q_w))\in\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\}
 \subseteq
 \{\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha},\ 
   \mathcal M^\star\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\}.       \tag{1}
\]
Taking probabilities, then the infimum over \(\mathfrak M_H\), and finally the lower limit proves the asserted uniform outer coverage.  Because (1) uses only weak inequalities and inclusion, simultaneous Hall equalities and arbitrary policy ties require no separate regularity condition.

We next give an explicit two-law obstruction to uniformly shrinking whole-set inference.  Fix \(H\ge2\), put \(\epsilon_n=n^{-2}>0\), and construct two laws with \(\mathsf P(R=1)=1/2\), no death, \(S_k^0=S_k^1=1\), \(B=0\), and switched residual \(W=0\).  Under law zero set \(T=0\) almost surely; under law one set \(T=H\) almost surely.  Give the standard sustained branch raw residual zero.  Observe every subject through \(k\); independently of the response tree and assignment, set \(C=K\) with probability \(\epsilon_n\) and \(C=k\) otherwise.  The only nonunit censoring continuation probability is \(\epsilon_n>0\).  Independence gives factual-arm sequential coarsening at random, assignment is independent of the response tree, assignment and landmark survival are positive, and \(B+W=0\le H\).  The cap-fibre lift in \(\text{thm:causal-response-tree-lift}\) completes legal raw-count branches while preserving the observed pushforward.  Thus both laws lie in \(\mathfrak M_H\); no uniform overlap constant has been added.

For every \(m\in\mathcal M\subseteq\{1,\ldots,H\}\), \(B<m\) and \(\pi=1\).  Hence the two sharp value sets are
\[
 V_0=\{(0)_{m\in\mathcal M}\},\qquad
 V_1=\{(H)_{m\in\mathcal M}\}.                           \tag{2}
\]
Couple one observation under the two laws using the same assignment, censoring draw, and all histories through \(k\).  Coupled observations can differ only when \(R=1\) and \(C=K\), an event of probability \(\epsilon_n/2\).  Coordinatewise coupling of \(n\) observations and the union bound give
\[
 \lVert P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}-P_{1,n}^{\otimes n}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le n\epsilon_n/2=(2n)^{-1}\longrightarrow0.             \tag{3}
\]

Let \(\mathcal C_n\) be any observed-data random region with uniform asymptotic whole-value-set coverage at level \(1-\alpha\).  Applied to the two triangular sequences, uniform honesty gives
\[
 P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}(V_0\subseteq\mathcal C_n)\ge1-\alpha-o(1),\qquad
 P_{1,n}^{\otimes n}(V_1\subseteq\mathcal C_n)\ge1-\alpha-o(1).        \tag{4}
\]
Total variation in (3) transfers the second event to law zero with an \(o(1)\) loss.  A union bound under law zero then gives
\[
 P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}\{V_0\cup V_1\subseteq\mathcal C_n\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-o(1).                                      \tag{5}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{diam}_{\infty}(\mathcal C_n)\ge H\) by (2), proving the whole-value-set obstruction.

For the optimizer obstruction, set \(H=3\), \(\mathcal M=\{1,2,3\}\), and use the common \((p,q)\) margins of \(\mathsf E_3\).  Their nontrivial Hall slacks are \((1/5,3/10,1/5)\), so a legal capacity coupling exists with strict slack.  In law zero put \(T=0\) in every row.  Capacity forces row \(b=3\) into column zero, so \(J_3=0\) under every compatible coupling, and nonnegativity gives \(J_1,J_2\ge0\).  Therefore \(R_3=0\).  The feasible plan
\[
 x_{00}=\frac15,\quad x_{03}=\frac15,\quad
 x_{11}=\frac1{10},\quad x_{12}=\frac15,\quad
 x_{21}=\frac15,\quad x_{30}=\frac1{10}                  \tag{6}
\]
has the required row and column margins, satisfies \(b+w\le3\), and yields
\((J_1,J_2,J_3)=(7/10,1/5,0)\).  Hence
\(R_1\ge D_{13}\ge7/10\) and \(R_2\ge D_{23}\ge1/5\), proving
\[
 \mathcal M^\star_0=\{3\}.                               \tag{7}
\]

In law one, conditional on \(B=1\), put probabilities \(5/6\) and \(1/6\) on \(T=1\) and \(T=2\); conditional on \(B=2\), put probabilities \(1/8\) and \(7/8\) on \(T=0\) and \(T=1\); and set \(T=0\) in rows zero and three.  Multiplication by the row masses gives
\[
 (\mu_0,\mu_1,\mu_2,\mu_3)=(0,7/20,7/40,0),              \tag{8}
\]
so \(\text{prop:rational-recommendation-reversal}\) gives
\(\mathcal M^\star_1=\{1\}\).  The common \(p\) margin permits identical pre-landmark intensive histories, and the standard sustained histories and switched margins can also be identical.  The response-tree lift supplies all unused branches.  Under the same censoring scheme the coupled observations can again differ only when \(R=1,C=K\), so (3) remains valid.

Let \(\mathcal K_n\subseteq\mathcal M\) be any uniformly honest outer confidence set for \(\mathcal M^\star\).  Coverage of the two unique optimizers, total-variation transfer, and the union bound give
\[
 P_{0,n}^{\otimes n}\{\{1,3\}\subseteq\mathcal K_n\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-o(1).                                      \tag{9}
\]
The two laws have strict Hall slack and unique optimizers; their only vanishing information is the probability \(\epsilon_n\) of observing post-landmark intensive outcomes.  Since \(\epsilon_n\) is positive for each \(n\), the sequence lies in the pointwise-overlap class \(\mathfrak M_H\), but it is excluded from every submodel imposing a fixed positive lower bound on factual censoring continuation.  This proves the claimed limitation.

added_lemmas.statement:
For each arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), let \(h_{0:K}\) be an absorbing recurrent-event history atom having positive probability under the sustained-arm law, and let \(d(h)=\min\{\ell:D_\ell(h)=1\}\), with \(d(h)=K\) if death does not occur by \(K\).  Define the observed at-risk kernels
\[
 \kappa_0^a(h_0)=\mathsf P(O_0=h_0\mid R=a),
 \qquad
 \kappa_\ell^a(h_\ell\mid h_{0:\ell-1})
 =\mathsf P(O_\ell=h_\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell,
                    O_{0:\ell-1}=h_{0:\ell-1})
\]
for \(1\le\ell\le d(h)\).  Under baseline randomization, consistency, factual-arm sequential coarsening at random, assignment positivity, and factual at-risk censoring positivity,
\[
 \mathsf P(\mathcal H_K^a=h_{0:K})
 =\kappa_0^a(h_0)
   \prod_{\ell=1}^{d(h)}
       \kappa_\ell^a(h_\ell\mid h_{0:\ell-1}),
\]
where every factor after an earlier absorbing death is the deterministic factor one.  Thus the complete sustained-arm history law is identified atom by atom from the distribution of \(O\).  Consequently
\[
 r_{bt}=\mathsf P(S_k^1=1,B=b,T=t),\qquad
 \pi=\sum_{b,t}r_{bt},\qquad p_{bt}=r_{bt}/\pi,
\]
and, writing \(\nu_w=\mathsf P(S_k^0=1,\min\{Z,H\}=w)\) and
\(\sigma_0=\mathsf P(S_k^0=1)\),
\[
 q_w=\nu_w/\sigma_0
\]
are observed-law functionals.  The two divisions are valid by landmark-survival positivity.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(a\) and a positive-probability absorbing atom \(h=h_{0:K}\).  For an alive prefix \(h_{0:\ell-1}\), put
\[
 g_\ell^a(h_{0:\ell-1})
 =\mathsf P(C\ge\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,
       D_{\ell-1}^a=0,\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a=h_{0:\ell-1}).       \tag{1}
\]
Factual-arm censoring positivity makes (1) strictly positive on every prefix of the chosen atom.  Sequential coarsening at random states, without suppressing its conditioning set, that
\[
 \mathsf P(C\ge\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,D_{\ell-1}^a=0,
                  \mathcal H_K^a=h)
 =g_\ell^a(h_{0:\ell-1}).                                  \tag{2}
\]
The chain rule and (2) give, for each \(j\le d(h)\),
\[
 \mathsf P(C\ge j\mid R=a,\mathcal H_K^a=h)
 =\prod_{\ell=1}^{j}g_\ell^a(h_{0:\ell-1}).                \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the \(\ell\)-th factor in the conditional chain rule is exactly (2).  The right side of (3), conditional on the prefix \(h_{0:j-1}\), does not depend on \(h_j,\ldots,h_K\).  Hence, for any supported alive prefix,
\[
 C\ge j\ \perp\!\!\!\perp\
 (\mathcal H_j^a,\ldots,\mathcal H_K^a)
 \mid R=a,\mathcal H_{j-1}^a.                              \tag{4}
\]
This conclusion has been derived from the displayed sequential restriction; no independence of censoring from the whole response tree has been added.

Now use Bayes' rule at an alive prefix.  By (2), (4), and the strict positivity of (1),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\mathsf P(\mathcal H_\ell^a=h_{0:\ell}
      \mid R=a,C\ge\ell,\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a=h_{0:\ell-1})\\
 &\quad=
 \frac{g_\ell^a(h_{0:\ell-1})
       \mathsf P(\mathcal H_\ell^a=h_{0:\ell}
          \mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,
                 \mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a=h_{0:\ell-1})}
      {g_\ell^a(h_{0:\ell-1})}\\
 &\quad=
 \mathsf P(\mathcal H_\ell^a=h_{0:\ell}
      \mid R=a,\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a=h_{0:\ell-1}).
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{5}
\]
The last equality follows from (4) with \(j=\ell-1\); for \(\ell=1\), the event \(C\ge0\) is certain.  Baseline randomization gives
\[
 \mathsf P(\mathcal H_K^a=h)=
 \mathsf P(\mathcal H_K^a=h\mid R=a),                      \tag{6}
\]
and consistency identifies every left side of (5), on \(R=a\) and \(C\ge\ell\), with the corresponding observed transition of \(O\).  Assignment positivity and (1) ensure that each observed conditional probability is well defined.  Applying the ordinary finite chain rule to (6), substituting (5), and stopping at the first death yields
\[
 \mathsf P(\mathcal H_K^a=h)
 =\kappa_0^a(h_0)
   \prod_{\ell=1}^{d(h)}
       \kappa_\ell^a(h_\ell\mid h_{0:\ell-1}).            \tag{7}
\]
Absorbing death makes every later coordinate deterministic, so no post-death censoring division is used.

The finite-horizon raw history space is countable because each count coordinate is in \(\mathbb Z_+\).  Therefore (7) identifies the law of the sustained history by countable summation of its atoms.  Summing the intensive-arm atoms over the event
\(\{S_k^1=1,B=b,T=t\}\) gives
\[
 r_{bt}=\mathsf P(S_k^1=1,B=b,T=t)=\pi p_{bt}.             \tag{8}
\]
Summing (8) over \(b,t\) gives \(\pi\), and landmark-survival positivity gives \(\pi>0\), so \(p_{bt}=r_{bt}/\pi\).  Likewise, summing standard-arm atoms gives
\[
 \nu_w=\mathsf P(S_k^0=1,\min\{Z,H\}=w),\qquad
 \sigma_0=\sum_w\nu_w=\mathsf P(S_k^0=1)>0.              \tag{9}
\]
The definition of conditional probability then gives \(q_w=\nu_w/\sigma_0\).  Equations (7)--(9) prove every asserted identification map.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a real matrix \(A\) and norms on its domain and codomain.  There is a constant \(c_A>0\), depending only on \(A\) and the norms, such that, whenever \(\{y:Ay\le b\}\) is nonempty, every \(x\) admits \(x_0\) with \(Ax_0\le b\) and
\[
 \lVert x-x_0\rVert\le c_A\lVert(Ax-b)_+\rVert.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: Let (1) be a consistent system of inequalities and let \(F_n\) and \(F_m\) each satisfy (3). Then there exists a constant \(c>0\) such that for any \(x\) there exists a solution \(x_0\) of (1) with \(F_n(x-x_0)\) at most \(cF_m((Ax-b)^+)\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(H\), \(K\), and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\).  Uniformly over triangular law--estimator sequences satisfying \(\operatorname{QIR}_{H,K,\varepsilon}(\mathsf P,\mathfrak I)\), the cross-fitted longitudinal estimators in \(\text{def:uniform-inference-handle}\) obey a joint asymptotic-linear expansion for the finite vector \(((r_{bt}),(q_w))\) with influence coordinates \(\varphi_{1,F_{bt}^1}\) and \(\varphi_{q_w}\).  The displayed Bonferroni--Chebyshev rectangle \(\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\) consequently has uniform simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) asymptotically and sup-norm diameter \(O(n^{-1/2})\).  The same probability statement simultaneously gives
\[
 \mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha},\qquad
 \mathcal M^\star\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha},\qquad
 \Delta^\star\subseteq\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha},
\]
without strict Hall slack, uniqueness, or exclusion of deterministic or randomized policy ties.  Uniformly on this quantitative submodel, the Hausdorff distance in sup norm between \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\) is \(O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2})\), and
\[
 \sup_{m\in\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}}
   \{R_m-\min_jR_j\}=O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \sup_{\delta\in\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha}}
   \{\mathcal R(\delta)-\inf_\lambda\mathcal R(\lambda)\}
   =O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2}).
\]
If additionally the nonoptimal deterministic regret gap is uniformly bounded below by a positive constant, then \(\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal M^\star\) with probability tending to one.  If additionally there is a constant \(c>0\) such that
\[
 \mathcal R(\delta)-\inf_\lambda\mathcal R(\lambda)
 \ge c\,\operatorname{dist}_1(\delta,\Delta^\star)
 \quad\text{for every }\delta\in\Delta_{\mathcal M}
\]
uniformly over the submodel, then
\(\sup_{\delta\in\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha}}
\operatorname{dist}_1(\delta,\Delta^\star)=O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2})\).  Without these gap or polyhedral-sharpness conditions, only simultaneous outer coverage and regret-excess contraction are asserted, so all ties remain admissible.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
We prove the claims in five steps.

\emph{Step 1: observed nuisances and the longitudinal score.}
For every terminal indicator in (2) of \(\text{def:uniform-inference-handle}\), \(\text{lem:observed-margin-identification}\) identifies every supported transition of the sustained arm.  Consequently it identifies the backward regressions \(Q_{\ell,F}^a\) and censoring hazards \(g_\ell^a\).  At a dead prefix the terminal value is already determined by absorption, so the recursion uses no unsupported continuation.

For the true nuisances, condition the \(\ell\)-th summand of \(\Psi_{a,F}\) first on \(R=a\), \(C\ge\ell-1\), and \(\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a\).  Sequential coarsening at random and consistency give
\[
 \mathsf E\!\left[
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{C\ge\ell,D_{\ell-1}^a=0\}}{\bar G_\ell^a}
 \{Q_{\ell,F}^a-Q_{\ell-1,F}^a\}
 \mathrel{\Big|} R=a,\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a\right]=0.       \tag{1}
\]
The division is valid because \(\operatorname{QIR}_{H,K,\varepsilon}\) gives \(\bar G_\ell^a\ge\varepsilon^\ell\) on the at-risk support.  Baseline randomization and \(g_a\ge\varepsilon\) then imply
\[
 \mathsf E\{\Psi_{a,F}(O)\}=\mathsf E\{Q_{0,F}^a(\mathcal H_0^a)\}=\theta_{a,F},
 \qquad \mathsf E(\varphi_{a,F})=0.                       \tag{2}
\]
Because \(0\le Q_{\ell,F}^a\le1\),
\[
 |\varphi_{a,F}|
 \le 2+K\varepsilon^{-(K+1)}=:C_0.                       \tag{3}
\]
Moreover \(\sigma_0\ge\varepsilon\), so (3) and the ratio formula give
\[
 |\varphi_{q_w}|\le 2C_0/\varepsilon=:C_{K,\varepsilon}. \tag{4}
\]
The latter constant also bounds the cell-mass influence coordinates after increasing it if necessary.

\emph{Step 2: cross-fitted asymptotic linearity.}
Consider one validation fold and condition on its training sample.  Add and subtract the score at the true nuisances:
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,F}-\theta_{a,F}
 =(\mathbb P_n-\mathsf P)\varphi_{a,F}
 +(\mathbb P_n-\mathsf P)\{\Psi_{a,F}(\widehat\eta)-\Psi_{a,F}(\eta)\}
 +\mathsf P\{\Psi_{a,F}(\widehat\eta)-\Psi_{a,F}(\eta)\}. \tag{5}
\]
Here \(\eta\) denotes the finite collection of true regressions and hazards.  Clipping and the overlap bounds make the score Lipschitz in each nuisance with a constant depending only on \(K\) and \(\varepsilon\).  Conditional variance in the validation fold and uniform \(L^2\)-consistency therefore give
\[
 (\mathbb P_n-\mathsf P)\{\Psi_{a,F}(\widehat\eta)-\Psi_{a,F}(\eta)\}
 =o_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2}).                                \tag{6}
\]
For completeness, iterated expectation in the last term of (5), followed by adding and subtracting each true backward regression, telescopes all terms that contain only a regression error or only a censoring error.  Cauchy--Schwarz leaves the explicit bound
\[
 \left|\mathsf P\{\Psi_{a,F}(\widehat\eta)-\Psi_{a,F}(\eta)\}\right|
 \le C(K,\varepsilon)
 \sum_{\ell=1}^{K}
 \lVert\widehat Q_{\ell-1,F}^a-Q_{\ell-1,F}^a\rVert_2
 \sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\lVert\widehat g_j^a-g_j^a\rVert_2.    \tag{7}
\]
To see why no first-order term is hidden in (7), the conditional mean of
\(Q_{\ell,F}^a-Q_{\ell-1,F}^a\) is zero by the defining backward recursion, while the conditional mean of the censoring indicator divided by its true continuation probability is one by sequential coarsening at random.  Thus every surviving summand contains one error of each kind.  The product-rate clause in \(\operatorname{QIR}_{H,K,\varepsilon}\) makes (7) \(o_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2})\).  Averaging the fixed number of folds in (5)--(7) proves, uniformly for all terminal indicators,
\[
 \widehat\theta_{a,F}-\theta_{a,F}
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\varphi_{a,F}(O_i)+o_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2}). \tag{8}
\]

Apply (8) to \(\nu_w\) and \(\sigma_0\).  Since \(\sigma_0\ge\varepsilon\) and \(\widehat\sigma_0\to\sigma_0\) uniformly, the clipped denominator equals \(\widehat\sigma_0\) with probability tending to one.  The exact ratio identity
\[
 \frac{\widehat\nu_w}{\widehat\sigma_0}-\frac{\nu_w}{\sigma_0}
 =\frac{(\widehat\nu_w-\nu_w)-q_w(\widehat\sigma_0-\sigma_0)}{\sigma_0}
 -\frac{(\widehat\sigma_0-\sigma_0)
 \{(\widehat\nu_w-\nu_w)-q_w(\widehat\sigma_0-\sigma_0)\}}
 {\sigma_0\widehat\sigma_0}                              \tag{9}
\]
and (8) show that the second term is \(O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1})\) and that the first has influence coordinate (3) of the definition.  This proves the asserted joint expansion.

\emph{Step 3: the simultaneous rectangle.}
Let \(\vartheta=((r_{bt}),(q_w))\) and \(d=(H+1)^2+(H+1)\).  For every coordinate \(s\) of the influence vector, (4) and Chebyshev's inequality give
\[
 \mathsf P\!\left(
 \left|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\varphi_s(O_i)\right|
 >C_{K,\varepsilon}\sqrt{\frac d{\alpha n}}\right)
 \le\frac\alpha d.                                      \tag{10}
\]
The union bound over the fixed \(d\) coordinates, (8)--(9), and uniformity of the remainders yield
\[
 \liminf_n\inf_{\operatorname{QIR}}
 \mathsf P\!\left\{
 \lVert\widehat\vartheta_n^{\mathrm{raw}}-\vartheta\rVert_\infty
 \le\frac{C_{K,\varepsilon}\sqrt{d/\alpha}+1}{\sqrt n}
 \right\}\ge1-\alpha.                                  \tag{11}
\]
The true margin vector belongs to the Hall-feasible projection domain.  If \(\widetilde\vartheta_n\) is a sup-norm projection of the raw estimate onto that domain, minimality and the triangle inequality give
\[
 \lVert\widetilde\vartheta_n-\vartheta\rVert_\infty
 \le2\lVert\widehat\vartheta_n^{\mathrm{raw}}-\vartheta\rVert_\infty. \tag{12}
\]
Thus the half-width (4) covers every true coordinate on the event in (11).  It is deterministic of order \(n^{-1/2}\), so the rectangle has the claimed sup-norm diameter.  Projection also ensures that the downstream confidence polytope is nonempty.

On the event of simultaneous margin coverage, \(\text{thm:confidence-polytope}\) gives
\(\mathcal V\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha}\) and
\(\mathcal M^\star\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\), while
\(\text{thm:randomized-confidence-polytope}\) gives
\(\Delta^\star\subseteq\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha}\).  These are set inclusions based on weak inequalities, so Hall equalities and all optimizer ties are retained.

\emph{Step 4: polyhedral contraction and regret excess.}
Write equivalently \(\vartheta=(\mathbf r,q)\), put \(\tau=\sum_{b,t}r_{bt}\), and
\(s_w=\tau q_w\).  By (12) and the width of the rectangle, every candidate
\((\mathbf r',\mathbf s')\) in its margin projection has positive total mass for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Indeed, if \(h_n\) is the common half-width and \(d_r=(H+1)^2\), its coordinatewise lower constraints give
\[
 \tau'=\sum_{b,t}r'_{bt}
 \ge\sum_{b,t}\max\{0,\widetilde r_{bt}-h_n\}
 \ge\varepsilon/2-d_rh_n\ge\varepsilon/4.                \tag{13}
\]
Define \(q'_w=s'_w/\tau'\).  The perspective inequalities in
\(\widehat{\mathcal P}_{n,\alpha}\) put every \(q'_w\) between the corresponding endpoints of \(\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\).  Hence
\[
 \lVert\mathbf r'-\mathbf r\rVert_\infty
 +\lVert\mathbf s'-\mathbf s\rVert_\infty
 =O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2})                                \tag{14}
\]
uniformly; the product \(s'_w=\tau' q'_w\) is Lipschitz because
\(0\le\tau',q'_w\le1\).  Encode nonnegativity, forbidden Ferrers cells, and the row and column equations of \(\mathsf X_H\) as one fixed finite inequality matrix \(A_H\).  Apply \(\text{lem:hoffman-polyhedral-error-bound}\) first to a candidate plan with the true right side and then to a true plan with the projected-center right side.  Since both right sides are feasible, it gives a constant \(L_H<\infty\), depending only on the fixed matrix, such that the correcting plans obey
\[
 \lVert\mathbf x'-\mathbf x\rVert_1
 \le L_H\{
 \lVert\mathbf r'-\mathbf r\rVert_1+
 \lVert\mathbf s'-\mathbf s\rVert_1\}.                  \tag{15}
\]
This is the only classical polyhedral sensitivity input; (13)--(14) are the note-specific perspective-margin calculation.

For every threshold, the value map is linear and \(0\le t,w\le H\).  Hence (14)--(15) imply
\[
 |\mathsf J_m(\mathbf r',\mathbf x')-
   \mathsf J_m(\mathbf r,\mathbf x)|
 \le H\lVert\mathbf r'-\mathbf r\rVert_1+
      H\lVert\mathbf x'-\mathbf x\rVert_1
 =O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2}).                               \tag{16}
\]
The two applications of (15) prove both directed Hausdorff bounds, so (16), uniformly over the finite menu, proves the asserted Hausdorff contraction of value sets.

If two compact value sets are within \(e\) in sup-norm Hausdorff distance, then directly from the support definition
\[
 |h_V(\lambda)-h_{V'}(\lambda)|
 \le e\lVert\lambda\rVert_1.                             \tag{17}
\]
Every deterministic pairwise direction and every randomized regret direction has \(\ell^1\)-norm at most two.  Taking finite maxima in (17) therefore shows that every candidate deterministic or randomized regret differs uniformly from its true counterpart by
\(e_n=O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2})\).  If
\(m\in\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\), the defining envelope inequality gives
\[
 R_m\le\underline R_m^{n,\alpha}+e_n
 \le\min_j\overline R_j^{n,\alpha}+e_n
 \le\min_jR_j+2e_n.                                     \tag{18}
\]
Likewise, if \(\delta\in\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha}\),
\[
 \mathcal R(\delta)
 \le\underline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\delta)+e_n
 \le\inf_\lambda\overline{\mathcal R}_{n,\alpha}(\lambda)+e_n
 \le\inf_\lambda\mathcal R(\lambda)+2e_n.               \tag{19}
\]
Equations (18)--(19) are the two regret-excess conclusions.

\emph{Step 5: exactly when geometric optimizer contraction follows.}
Suppose the deterministic gap
\[
 \inf_{\operatorname{QIR}}
 \min_{m\notin\mathcal M^\star}
 \{R_m-\min_jR_j\}>0.                                   \tag{20}
\]
Then (18) excludes every nonoptimizer with probability tending to one, proving
\(\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal M^\star\).  For mixtures, the stated polyhedral-sharpness inequality and (19) give
\[
 \sup_{\delta\in\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha}}
 \operatorname{dist}_1(\delta,\Delta^\star)
 \le 2e_n/c=O_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2}).                      \tag{21}
\]
Without (20) or the sharpness inequality, (18)--(19) control loss but not distance to a possibly flat optimizer face.  The proof therefore does not convert a Hall or policy tie into an unstated separation assumption.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For a bounded terminal full-history functional \(F\) in arm \(a\), put \(\theta_{a,F}=\mathsf E\{F(\mathcal H_K^a)\}\), \(g_a=\mathsf P(R=a)\), and
\[
 g_\ell^a(h)=\mathsf P(C\ge\ell\mid R=a,C\ge\ell-1,
 D_{\ell-1}^a=0,\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a=h),
 \qquad
 \bar G_\ell^a=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell}g_j^a(\mathcal H_{j-1}^a).
\]
Set \(Q_{K,F}^a=F\).  Backwards over supported alive histories, set
\[
 Q_{\ell-1,F}^a(h)=
 \mathsf E\{Q_{\ell,F}^a(\mathcal H_\ell^a)
       \mid \mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a=h\},
\]
and on a dead history use the deterministic absorbing completion.  Define
\[
 \Psi_{a,F}(O)=
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{R=a\}}{g_a}\left[Q_{0,F}^a(\mathcal H_0^a)+
 \sum_{\ell=1}^{K}
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{C\ge\ell,D_{\ell-1}^a=0\}}{\bar G_\ell^a}
 \{Q_{\ell,F}^a(\mathcal H_\ell^a)-Q_{\ell-1,F}^a(\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a)\}\right],
 \qquad
 \varphi_{a,F}=\Psi_{a,F}-\theta_{a,F}.                    \tag{1}
\]
Use the terminal cell indicators
\[
 F_{bt}^1=\mathbf 1\{S_k^1=1,B=b,T=t\},\qquad
 F_w^0=\mathbf 1\{S_k^0=1,\min\{Z,H\}=w\},\qquad
 F_S^0=\mathbf 1\{S_k^0=1\}.                              \tag{2}
\]
Then \(r_{bt}=\theta_{1,F_{bt}^1}\), \(\nu_w=\theta_{0,F_w^0}\), \(\sigma_0=\theta_{0,F_S^0}\), \(q_w=\nu_w/\sigma_0\), and the ratio influence function is
\[
 \varphi_{q_w}=\frac{\varphi_{0,F_w^0}-q_w\varphi_{0,F_S^0}}{\sigma_0}. \tag{3}
\]
The procedure \(\mathfrak I\) uses a fixed number of folds.  On each validation fold it evaluates (1) with backward regressions and censoring hazards fitted only on the complementary training folds, with regressions clipped to \([0,1]\) and hazards clipped to \([\varepsilon/2,1]\), and averages the resulting scores.  For \(q_w\), it divides the cross-fitted numerator estimate by the maximum of the corresponding survival-denominator estimate and \(\varepsilon/2\).  Let \(\widehat\vartheta_n^{\mathrm{raw}}\) collect these estimates of \(((r_{bt}),(q_w))\), and let \(\widetilde\vartheta_n\) be a sup-norm projection onto the compact set of Hall-feasible margin pairs having intensive-survivor mass at least \(\varepsilon/2\). \[
 \frac{2\{C_{K,\varepsilon}\sqrt{d/\alpha}+1\}}{\sqrt n},              \tag{4}
\]
clipped to \([0,1]\).  The endpoints in (4) define \(\mathcal I_{n,\alpha}\), which is then inverted through \(\widehat{\mathcal P}_{n,\alpha}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_{n,\alpha}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal M}_{n,\alpha}\), and \(\widehat\Delta_{n,\alpha}\).  This definition introduces no quantitative restriction into \(\mathfrak M_H\); its positive rate guarantee is conditional on \(\operatorname{QIR}_{H,K,\varepsilon}\).

proposed.comparator_claim: Assumption 1 supplies the published uncapped residual no-carry-over equality, Proposition 1 supplies threshold-wise scalar bounds, and the decision section compares deterministic switching regimes.

The paper formulates factual-arm sequential coarsening at random and develops influence-function and multiply robust estimation for its recurrent-event mean and survival functionals; it does not state identification of the entire sustained-history law or the finite vector used here.
The paper characterizes atom-sensitive sharp bounds for the distribution of an unrestricted sum with fixed marginals.

Theorem 4 characterizes nonempty fixed-margin staircase transportation classes by critical-position inequalities, and Section 3 gives constructions; Theorem 1 is the general arbitrary-pattern support antecedent.
The paper gives greedy optimization results for staircase transportation problems with structured rewards.
The paper shows that the joint geometry of partially identified treatment payoffs governs minimax-regret rules and their randomization.
The paper formulates compatibility of causal marginal models with a single global structural causal model.
The paper obtains confidence regions for identified sets by inverting criterion functions under moment equalities and inequalities.
The paper develops regularized support-function inference for polygonal affine identified sets with changing active faces.

prose_updates.tldr: A randomized recurrent-event trial identifies separately capped baseline and residual margins while leaving their dependence unknown, and the raw recurrent paths remain unbounded. The externally prespecified sensitivity restriction \(B+W\le H\) creates a Ferrers transport problem and is not implied by separate capping. The cap-fibre response-tree construction proves every feasible triple coupling attainable, including in the published raw no-carry-over subclass. Exact endpoints and the common-law value polytope yield deterministic and randomized minimax regret and the cap-three recommendation reversal. For inference, a direct sequential-factorization proof now identifies every supported sustained-history atom and hence \((r_{bt},q_w)\); on the explicit quantitative-overlap and cross-fitted product-rate submodel, a longitudinal AIPW Bonferroni rectangle contracts at root-\(n\) rate and its perspective inversion covers the whole value set and every deterministic or randomized robust optimizer, including ties. On the broader pointwise-overlap class \(\mathfrak M_H\), uniformly shrinking inference remains impossible by the vanishing-information two-law construction. Thus the positive quantitative theorem and the negative base-class theorem have disjoint, explicit scopes.

project_justification.gap: The closest recurrent-event switching analysis supplies an uncapped no-carry-over equality, scalar sharp bounds, and deterministic decision criteria. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 supplies the factual-arm sequential-CAR setup and influence-function architecture for recurrent-event mean and survival targets, but not an atom-by-atom identification theorem for the complete sustained history, the capped margin vector used here, shared-law deterministic and randomized regret inversion, or the positive-versus-negative uniform-inference boundary. Dahl2008 supplies staircase feasibility only.
project_justification.fill: The formal kernel combines the attributed staircase feasibility certificate with an explicit raw-path cap-fibre lift, derives the complete common-law value and regret geometry, and proves the missing inference chain. Sequential CAR and positivity give a finite product of observed transition kernels for every supported absorbing history atom. Explicit backward regressions, cumulative censoring hazards, longitudinal AIPW and ratio influence functions, cross-fitting, Hall-feasible projection, and conservative simultaneous inversion give root-\(n\) value-set and regret-excess contraction on a quantitative regularity submodel. A separate two-law theorem proves that pointwise positivity in the unchanged base class cannot yield uniform shrinkage.

sampling_model.overlap: The maintained class assumes positive baseline assignment and positive arm-specific factual censoring continuation on every supported at-risk history, with no positivity for the unsupported switch. The positive inference submodel separately fixes \(H\), \(K\), and \(\varepsilon>0\) and requires assignment, landmark survival, and every supported factual continuation probability to be at least \(\varepsilon\); the base class itself is unchanged.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Every sustained-history atom is identified by a proved product of observed at-risk transition kernels. The finite cell vector is estimated by cross-fitted longitudinal AIPW scores for intensive cell indicators and by numerator, survival-denominator, and ratio scores for the standard residual margin. Clipped, uniformly consistent backward-regression and censoring-hazard fits with \(o_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2})\) regression--censoring error products yield a root-\(n\) simultaneous rectangle on the quantitative submodel. Hall-feasible projection keeps its confidence polytope nonempty. Under pointwise overlap alone, the vanishing-information impossibility still applies.

prose_updates.related_work: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 supplies the uncapped residual no-carry-over equality and threshold-wise scalar analysis. The cap-fibre construction here transfers sharpness after intersecting that class with \(B+W\le H\). Dahl2008 supplies the reindexed staircase feasibility criterion, and Hoffman1952 supplies only the fixed-matrix polyhedral error bound used for the new perspective-Lipschitz argument. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 is used for the factual-arm sequential-CAR formulation and motivates longitudinal influence-function estimation; it does not assert identification of the entire sustained-history law. That law is derived here atom by atom from randomization, consistency, sequential CAR, and positivity, then specialized to \(r_{bt}\) and the numerator--denominator representation of \(q_w\). ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, AndrewsSoares2010, and Gafarov2025 motivate inference with binding inequalities and changing faces. The present positive result is a finite-dimensional conservative cross-fitted inversion under quantitative overlap, while the headline two-point theorem shows why the same conclusion is impossible uniformly under pointwise overlap. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026 motivates the decision relevance of the shared payoff set and randomization.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The cap \(H\) constrains only the separately capped summaries and never the primitive raw recurrent counts. Its clinical mechanism is not established for SPRINT. The response-tree lift preserves factual-arm sequential censoring without assuming censoring independence from the whole response tree. The positive inference theorem is not a consequence of the maintained class: it uses a separate quantitative predicate with uniform assignment, survival, and factual censoring overlap and explicit nuisance product rates. The conservative Bonferroni--Chebyshev rectangle establishes uniform root-\(n\) order but does not claim semiparametric efficiency or shortest width. At Hall and policy ties, outer coverage and regret-excess contraction remain valid, but optimizer-set distance need not contract without the displayed gap or polyhedral-sharpness condition. The broad-class impossibility sequences violate every fixed quantitative overlap bound and therefore do not contradict the positive submodel theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved scope includes exact endpoints, an observed-law-preserving raw-path causal lift, sharp transfer to the published raw no-carry-over subclass intersected with the cap, the complete common-law value set, deterministic and randomized minimax regret, and confidence-polytope inversion. Complete sustained-arm history identification is now proved directly by a finite observed-kernel product, rather than attributed to a source that identifies only particular functionals. Positive root-\(n\) margin, value-set, and regret-excess contraction holds only on the explicit quantitative inference regularity submodel with fixed \(H,K\), a fixed overlap lower bound, cross-fitting, clipped uniformly consistent nuisances, and longitudinal product-rate control. All deterministic and randomized ties retain simultaneous outer coverage. Geometric optimizer contraction is claimed only under an additional uniform deterministic regret gap or randomized polyhedral-sharpness inequality. On the unchanged pointwise-overlap class, uniformly honest regions need not shrink, as witnessed by the stated two-law sequences. SPRINT remains only a conditional capped-loss consumer requiring an externally defended cap at \(k=300\) and a feasible censoring-adjusted Hall system.

statement_notes.justification: This lemma repairs the inferential foundation by deriving, rather than citing, the finite sequential factorization for every supported absorbing sustained-history atom.
statement_notes.gap: Published recurrent-event CAR results used here formulate the coarsening condition and identify particular mean or survival targets, not the complete history law needed for every capped terminal cell.
statement_notes.consumer: The explicit cell and ratio influence functions use the identified transition kernels to construct all backward outcome regressions.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives a computable positive inference result on exactly the quantitative submodel that excludes the headline vanishing-information sequences, and propagates root-\(n\) margin error through the transport geometry to values and decisions.
statement_notes.gap: Set-theoretic confidence inversion alone does not supply a first-stage construction, a contraction rate, or the regularity boundary under censoring; prior CAR and support-function literatures do not provide this capped recurrent-event composition.
statement_notes.consumer: A trial analysis satisfying prespecified quantitative overlap and cross-fitted nuisance-rate diagnostics can report one simultaneous region for all capped values and robust deterministic or randomized decisions, while retaining every tie.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem isolates the information-theoretic obstruction in the unchanged pointwise-overlap model by constructing total-variation-indistinguishable laws whose value sets or unique robust thresholds remain separated.
statement_notes.gap: Sequential CAR, pointwise positivity, and recurrent-event multiply robust estimation do not by themselves answer whether honest confidence regions can shrink uniformly when post-landmark observation probabilities approach zero.
statement_notes.consumer: Investigators must either verify a quantitative overlap and nuisance-rate submodel before using the positive cross-fitted result or report the broader-class nonshrinkage limitation; Hall slack and unique policies do not cure vanishing information.
